shadows.name: addon-render-shadow
shadows.value: In the 96-DPI qualified run, manifest defaults are shadowSize 24px and shadowOpacity 22%. Render uses a 12px box-blur radius and a 6px downward offset. The PNG alpha halo is Render output, not a DWM-only shadow measurement.
shadows.purpose: Shadow synthesized by add-on Render from the transformed captured-window alpha.

narrative.overview: This add-on extends MyWallpaper's usual settings surface and uses the host's native-only settings renderer. It has no separate settings identity. “Fluide et expressif” is the chosen motion default; it describes the effect preset, not a visual theme. The native sample canvas is defined in src/preview.cpp. The supplied PNGs are outputs from the add-on Render pass, based on that captured window image, under Windows 11 build 26200 at 96 DPI. They show animated image output after the add-on rounded mask and shadow handling, with optional contour processing; the qualified runtime frames use contour off. The caption chrome in the source image is Windows-drawn. They do not show the MyWallpaper sidebar, settings controls, or the preview controller and its buttons.
keyCharacteristics: Settings appearance is inherited from MyWallpaper; no add-on-specific settings palette or control styling was observed.
The sample canvas uses a deep navy field, cool light text, and a blue-to-sage bar series.
Windows supplies the caption chrome; the add-on renderer applies a rounded mask and shadow and can add a configurable contour to animation output.
dos: Do keep the preview tokens scoped to the native test canvas.
Do treat settings appearance as inherited from MyWallpaper until the host surface is visually observed.
Do distinguish Windows-drawn caption chrome from the add-on-rendered mask, optional contour, and shadow.
donts: Don't present the native-frame PNGs as captures of the MyWallpaper sidebar or its controls.
Don't infer settings colors, spacing, typography, hover, focus, or disabled states from the sample window.
Don't represent Windows controls with invented HTML or CSS snippets.
